messages:
Maya L: Anyone else seeing a spike in ALB target deregistrations in us-west-2 after the kube-proxy rollout? We dropped ~15 targets in the last 10m.
Raj P: seeing it too, started ~12:05Z. ALB access logs show 503 / connection resets to targets.
Samira: I pulled kube events — readiness probes are timing out (~10s) then pods marked Unhealthy and ALB deregisters.
kevin: sample ALB access log line i pulled: `target:10.0.45.18:8080 target_status_code=- elb_status_code=503 received_bytes=0 sent_bytes=0 request_processing_time=0.00000 target_processing_time=0.00000 response_processing_time=0.00000`
Maya L: also seeing NAT nodes with very high ephemeral port usage, conntrack nearing capacity.
Raj P: ran `sudo conntrack -S` — tcp entries ~95k, nf_conntrack_max = 100000 on several nodes.
Samira: reminder — we rolled a kube-proxy image + iptables->nft fallback 12m before the first dereg. Could be related to port allocation behavior.
kevin: checked ip-masq-agent configmap, nothing obvious changed in nonMasqueradeCIDR, but ports look default (32768-61000). No explicit preservePorts setting.
Raj P: hypothesis: high outbound concurrency + tight SNAT port pool + conntrack TTL causing source-port collisions. If responses go to the wrong tuple the target RSTs or connections drop, ALB sees that as unhealthy.
Maya L: can someone run on a NAT node: `ss -tn sport >= :32768` — I did `ss -tn sport > 32767 | wc -l` => 58k established/close-wait/etc.
Samira: mitigation plan: 1) increase nf_conntrack_max, 2) expand SNAT port range on nodes, 3) roll back kube-proxy change until we understand port behavior, 4) throttle healthcheck concurrency if possible.
kevin: I bumped nf_conntrack_max -> 262144 on the two busiest NAT nodes and reverted kube-proxy to previous image at 12:20Z. Watching for evictions.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0318-33 — ALB target deregistrations (us-west-2).
Raj P: opened AWS support case and attached tcpdump showing SYN from ALB, SYN/ACK from target, then later a RST with unexpected tuple. AWS confirmed they see replies hitting an unexpected 4-tuple if source port is reused.
Maya L: after conntrack bump + rollback, deregistration rate dropped to near zero over the next 15m. Looks like a port exhaustion/tuple-reuse issue.
Samira: filed a runbook PR with checks and alerts: conntrack usage, ephemeral port utilization, and automated scaling of NAT nodes when >80% ephemeral ports in use. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/412
Olivia: thanks — can we also add a note to infra docs recommending NLB ip-target mode or static IP targets for services that receive heavy ALB healthchecks?
Maya L: agreed. Follow-up actions: increase SNAT port pool in our AMI, add ephemeral-port alerting, harden ip-masq-agent config, and schedule a postmortem. Assigning to Samira + Raj.
Samira: will draft postmortem, include timeline and remediation.
Olivia: scheduling a 30m retro tomorrow 10:00 PT. I'll page infra owners if it flares overnight.
Maya L: closing the thread for now — great catch everyone :thumbsup:
